problems.source_says: The score counts dictionary categories in each participant's own generated explanations of the business problem. This measures within-person category breadth and therefore maps to flexibility under codebook section 6. It is not a comparison across people; question = with_ai, measure = category_count, and unit = participant remain supported. Only the Full arm had AI while these problem formulations were produced.
problems.quote: “Count” indicates the number of categories covered by the problem formulation.
problems.locator: PDF p. 91 (printed appendix p. 48), Table E.5 col. 1 and note; PDF p. 84, Appendix E.2.1; PDF p. 55, Table A.2 problem-formulation instructions; PDF p. 13, Section 3.1; creativity-codebook.md section 6, lines 81 and 87.

problems.source_says: The paper explicitly defines broad versus specific articulation by the level of contextual detail in an individual option, then aggregates the classifications to each participant's proportion of broad options. Codebook section 6 defines elaboration as detail or length of a single output, so this is an elaboration measure. Retain the printed broadness coefficients unchanged; higher broadness corresponds to less elaboration. The with_ai question, automated classification procedure, and participant analysis unit are supported.
problems.quote: the broad vs. specific articulation (based on the level of contextual detail).
problems.locator: PDF p. 77 (printed appendix p. 34), Table D.4 note and Table D.5; PDF p. 76, Appendix D.2 classification and participant aggregation; creativity-codebook.md section 6, line 82.
